programme.displayName: Amazon SQS: Basic Message Queue Test
programme.subtitle: sqs-learning-path · Complete beginner replacement for published source revision 3
programme.description: A complete beginner-friendly Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) Follow Along in Europe (London) (eu-west-2). It uses two fixed, harmless queues: sqs-basic-test-standard and sqs-basic-test-orders.fifo.
programme.learningOutcome: Use the Amazon SQS console and separate AWS CLI commands to verify access, create standard and FIFO queues, send, receive, delete, delay, and verify harmless test messages, then manually delete only the queues created in this Follow Along.

phases.title: Access and standard-queue basics
phases.description: Confirm Amazon SQS access in Europe (London), create one standard queue, and complete the basic send, receive, and delete lifecycle.

phases.title: Standard-queue delivery settings
phases.description: Edit the standard queue’s timing and payload settings, test a harmless delayed message, and use long polling.

tasks.title: 1. Verify Amazon SQS Console Access in eu-west-2
tasks.feature: Amazon SQS console access and regional queue list
tasks.goal: Open Amazon SQS in Europe (London) and confirm that the Queues page is available to the approved lab identity.
tasks.whyItMatters: Amazon SQS queues are regional resources. Keeping all work in eu-west-2 ensures that the queue URLs, Console view, and CLI commands refer to the same Region.

consoleSteps.title: Select the lab Region
consoleSteps.instruction: In the navigation bar, choose the Region selector.

instructions.text: In the navigation bar, choose the Region selector.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The console shows Europe (London) as the selected Region.
consoleSteps.warning: Use eu-west-2 throughout this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Open Amazon SQS

instructions.text: Choose Queues in the navigation pane.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Queues page is visible in Europe (London).
consoleSteps.warning: Use an approved non-root lab identity.

cliSteps.explanation: Lists the queue URLs that the configured, authorized CLI identity can access in Europe (London).
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns QueueUrls when accessible queues exist, or an empty result when none exist.
cliSteps.warning: This command requires preconfigured authorized CLI authentication. Do not create or expose credentials for this Follow Along.

verification.title: Confirm the regional queue view
verification.instruction: Verify that the Amazon SQS Queues page remains open with Europe (London) selected.
verification.expectedResult: You can continue the Follow Along in eu-west-2.

verification.title: Confirm CLI access
verification.instruction: Review the result of the list-queues command.
verification.expectedResult: The command completes without an authorization error.

tasks.title: 2. Create a Standard Test Queue and Record Its Identifiers
tasks.goal: Create the standard queue named sqs-basic-test-standard and identify its queue URL and ARN.
tasks.whyItMatters: A queue URL identifies the queue for SQS API and CLI operations. A standard queue is appropriate when strict ordering is not required.

consoleSteps.title: Start standard-queue creation
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The queue name field contains sqs-basic-test-standard.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not include confidential information in a queue name.

consoleSteps.title: Create the queue
consoleSteps.instruction: Leave the default Configuration values unchanged.

instructions.text: Leave the default Configuration values unchanged.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The sqs-basic-test-standard Details page opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Queue type cannot be changed after creation.

consoleSteps.title: Record queue identifiers
consoleSteps.instruction: Copy the Queue URL from the Details page.

instructions.text: Copy the Queue URL from the Details page.
Copy the Queue ARN from the Details page.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: You have recorded the URL and ARN for sqs-basic-test-standard.
consoleSteps.warning: Use the queue URL, not the queue name, in later CLI commands.

cliSteps.explanation: Creates the standard test queue. Omitting the FifoQueue attribute creates a standard queue.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns QueueUrl for sqs-basic-test-standard.
cliSteps.warning: If this queue name already exists with different attributes, Amazon SQS can return an error.

cliSteps.explanation: Retrieves the ARN for the standard queue. Replace <standard-queue-url-from-create-queue> with the QueueUrl returned by the immediately preceding create-queue command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns the QueueArn attribute.
cliSteps.warning: The placeholder is required because the account-specific queue URL is returned only after queue creation.

verification.title: Verify the standard queue in the Console
verification.instruction: On the sqs-basic-test-standard Details page, verify that the queue name is sqs-basic-test-standard and the Type is Standard.
verification.expectedResult: The intended standard queue is displayed.

verification.title: Verify the queue URL from the CLI
verification.instruction: Review the QueueUrl returned by create-queue.

tasks.title: 3. Send, Receive, Inspect, and Delete a Standard-Queue Message
tasks.goal: Send one harmless message, poll for it, inspect the visible message details, and explicitly delete it.
tasks.whyItMatters: Receiving a message does not delete it. A consumer must explicitly delete a successfully processed message using its receipt handle.

consoleSteps.title: Open message actions
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Send and receive messages page opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Send only the fixed harmless sample message.

consoleSteps.title: Send the sample message
consoleSteps.instruction: Enter SQS basic test message in Message body.

instructions.text: Enter SQS basic test message in Message body.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A success message and sent-message details are visible.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not enter personal, confidential, or production data.

consoleSteps.title: Poll for the message
consoleSteps.expectedResult: A message appears in Messages with its Message ID, sent date, size, and receive count.
consoleSteps.warning: A queue with few messages can occasionally return an empty response; poll again if necessary.

consoleSteps.title: Delete the processed message

instructions.text: Choose Delete in the Delete Messages dialog box.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The selected message is removed from the Messages list.
consoleSteps.warning: Delete only the fixed test message created by this Follow Along.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --message-body "SQS basic test message" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Sends the fixed harmless message to the standard queue. Replace <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> with the queue URL recorded in Task 2.
cliSteps.warning: The placeholder is the QueueUrl produced in Task 2.

cliSteps.explanation: Receives an available message and returns its message-system attributes and receipt handle. Replace the placeholder with the Task 2 queue URL.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns a Messages array containing MessageId, Body, Attributes, and ReceiptHandle when a message is available.
cliSteps.warning: Record the ReceiptHandle from this receive result for the next command.

cliSteps.explanation: Permanently deletes the received message. The queue URL comes from Task 2 and the receipt handle comes from the preceding receive-message result.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output when deletion succeeds.
cliSteps.warning: A receipt handle is temporary; use the one returned by the immediately preceding receive operation.

verification.title: Verify Console deletion
verification.instruction: Choose Poll for messages after deleting the selected test message.
verification.expectedResult: The deleted test message is not displayed.

verification.title: Verify CLI deletion
verification.instruction: Run the receive-message command again after delete-message.
verification.expectedResult: The deleted test message is not returned.

tasks.title: 4. Configure a Delayed Message and Long Polling
tasks.feature: Amazon SQS queue parameters and delayed messages
tasks.goal: Set safe test values for queue retention, delivery delay, maximum message size, and long polling, then send one delayed test message.
tasks.whyItMatters: Queue-level attributes control when messages become available, how long they remain available for processing, how large they can be, and how receive requests behave when no message is immediately available.

consoleSteps.title: Open queue configuration
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Configuration section is visible for sqs-basic-test-standard.
consoleSteps.warning: These edits apply only to the queue created in Task 2.

consoleSteps.title: Set retention

instructions.text: Choose Days for Message retention period.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Message retention period shows 1 Day.
consoleSteps.warning: Reducing retention can expire older messages.

consoleSteps.title: Set the queue delivery delay
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Delivery delay shows 0 Seconds.
consoleSteps.warning: The delayed-message test later uses a per-message delivery delay.

consoleSteps.title: Set maximum message size

instructions.text: Choose KiB for Maximum message size.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Maximum message size shows 1024 KiB.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use SQS for confidential payloads.

consoleSteps.title: Enable long polling
consoleSteps.instruction: Enter 20 in Receive message wait time.

instructions.text: Enter 20 in Receive message wait time.
Choose Seconds for Receive message wait time.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The queue Details page opens with the saved configuration.
consoleSteps.warning: Twenty seconds is the maximum long-polling wait time.

consoleSteps.title: Send a delayed sample message

instructions.text: Enter Delayed SQS test message in Message body.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A success message confirms that the delayed message was sent.
consoleSteps.warning: Wait at least 10 seconds before polling for this message.

consoleSteps.title: Receive and delete the delayed message

instructions.text: Choose Delete in the Delete Messages dialog box.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The delayed test message appears after its delay and is then deleted.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not delete messages that were not created by this Follow Along.

cliSteps.explanation: Sets one-day retention, no queue-level delay, a 1 MiB maximum message size, and a 20-second queue-level receive wait time. Replace the placeholder with the Task 2 queue URL.
cliSteps.warning: Attribute changes can take time to propagate. This command changes only sqs-basic-test-standard when the correct URL is supplied.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --message-body "Delayed SQS test message" --delay-seconds 10 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Sends one harmless message that becomes available after 10 seconds. Replace the placeholder with the Task 2 queue URL.
cliSteps.warning: Per-message delay is supported for standard queues and is limited to 900 seconds.

cliSteps.explanation: Uses a 20-second receive wait time to retrieve an available message or return when the wait time expires. Replace the placeholder with the Task 2 queue URL.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns the delayed message after it becomes available, or an empty result if no message becomes available during the wait.
cliSteps.warning: If a message is returned, delete it with a current receipt handle before cleanup.

verification.title: Verify saved queue settings
verification.instruction: On the queue Details page, verify the configured retention, delivery delay, maximum message size, and receive message wait time.
verification.expectedResult: The settings show 1 Day, 0 Seconds, 1024 KiB, and 20 Seconds.

verification.title: Verify long-poll receive behavior
verification.instruction: Review the receive-message command result after using --wait-time-seconds 20.
verification.expectedResult: The command waits for an available message or returns after its wait time expires.

tasks.title: 5. Create and Test a FIFO Queue
tasks.goal: Create sqs-basic-test-orders.fifo, send one harmless FIFO message with a message group ID, and verify that the queue uses FIFO-specific fields.
tasks.whyItMatters: FIFO queues are used when message order matters or duplicates cannot be tolerated. FIFO queue names must end with .fifo, and sent FIFO messages require a message group ID.

consoleSteps.title: Start FIFO-queue creation
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The queue form shows FIFO as the selected Type and sqs-basic-test-orders.fifo as the Name.
consoleSteps.warning: A FIFO queue name must end with .fifo.

consoleSteps.title: Create the FIFO queue
consoleSteps.instruction: Leave the default Configuration values unchanged.

instructions.text: Leave the default Configuration values unchanged.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The sqs-basic-test-orders.fifo Details page opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Queue type cannot be changed after creation.

consoleSteps.title: Send a FIFO test message

instructions.text: Enter FIFO SQS test message in Message body.
Enter test-order-group in Message group ID.
Enter fifo-test-message-001 in Message deduplication ID.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A success message confirms that the FIFO test message was sent.
consoleSteps.warning: FIFO queues do not support per-message delivery delays.

consoleSteps.title: Receive and delete the FIFO test message

instructions.text: Select the returned FIFO test message.
Choose Delete in the Delete Messages dialog box.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The FIFO test message is deleted.
consoleSteps.warning: Delete only the harmless FIFO test message created in this task.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs create-queue --queue-name sqs-basic-test-orders.fifo --attributes FifoQueue=true --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Creates the FIFO test queue. The FifoQueue attribute specifies FIFO queue type.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns QueueUrl for sqs-basic-test-orders.fifo.
cliSteps.warning: The .fifo suffix is required, and the queue type cannot be changed after creation.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <fifo-queue-url-from-create-queue> --message-body "FIFO SQS test message" --message-group-id test-order-group --message-deduplication-id fifo-test-message-001 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Sends a fixed harmless FIFO message. Replace <fifo-queue-url-from-create-queue> with the QueueUrl returned by the preceding create-queue command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns a MessageId and SequenceNumber.
cliSteps.warning: The FIFO queue URL is account-specific and is returned only after creation.

cliSteps.explanation: Receives the FIFO test message and returns its current receipt handle. Replace the placeholder with the FIFO QueueUrl.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns the FIFO test message and a ReceiptHandle when the message is available.
cliSteps.warning: Use the returned receipt handle immediately if deleting with the CLI.

cliSteps.explanation: Deletes the received FIFO test message. The queue URL comes from FIFO queue creation and the receipt handle comes from the immediately preceding receive-message result.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output when deletion succeeds.
cliSteps.warning: Do not reuse a receipt handle from an earlier receive operation.

verification.title: Verify FIFO queue type
verification.instruction: On the sqs-basic-test-orders.fifo Details page, verify that the queue name ends in .fifo and the Type is FIFO.
verification.expectedResult: The intended FIFO queue is displayed.

verification.title: Verify FIFO send result
verification.expectedResult: The result includes a MessageId and SequenceNumber.

warnings.cost: Amazon SQS requests can incur charges. This Follow Along creates only two small queues and sends only harmless test messages, but delete both queues after verification.
warnings.safety: Use only the fixed queue names and fixed sample messages in this package. Do not send personal, confidential, production, or regulated data. Delete only sqs-basic-test-standard and sqs-basic-test-orders.fifo.
warnings.credentials: Do not create, reveal, download, or share access keys. Console and CLI access must use an already approved authentication method.
warnings.region: Perform every regional Amazon SQS action in Europe (London), eu-west-2. Queue URLs are Region-specific.

findings.message: This replacement intentionally does not create an IAM user, access keys, an IAM policy, or a permissions boundary. Those actions are outside the Follow Along because the requested package must not include credentials or propose an IAM policy.

The official Amazon SQS documentation states that the Console visibility-timeout setting applies to all messages in a queue, while single-message visibility changes require an SDK. Therefore, this beginner Console journey does not claim to perform per-message ChangeMessageVisibility in the Console.

If the approved lab identity cannot open the Amazon SQS Queues page or the list-queues command returns an authorization error, an account administrator must review the existing approved access arrangement outside this Follow Along.
